text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA
- Schools and universities which suspended work cannot use funds from republican budget, says Serbian government.
- Participants at Serb-Croatian round table in Belgrade stress urgent solution of refugee problem which is both humanitarian and political.
- Yugoslavia-Macedonia sign protocol on transport cooperation in Belgrade.
- Yugoslav Airlines (JAT) opens one more direct line to Skopje, now has four flights a week.
- Pharmaceutical company ICN Yugoslavia (Galenika) and Swiss firm Hoffman La Roche sign cooperation agreement on three-year-use of licence.
- Any increase of exports will be coupled with further increase of imports, says Belgrade Foreign Trade Institute.
- We must continue ownership transformation but will not sell off property nor can we expect complex job to be completed rapidly, says president of Belgrade Chamber of Economy.
- Federal government determines payment operations bill transferring them from central service to banks and other financial institutions.
- Subscription ends for first issue of shares of Politika AD (51 million German marks). Good response of employees who subscribe shares worth six million German marks.
NASA BORBA

- Yugoslavia's cooperation with financial adviser London's Nat West Markets has completely stopped, a source said citing as one of the reasons the country's failure to listen to recommendations on privatisation of its PTT.
- Students continue protest marches greeted by citizens along the way. Paper awards them prize for tolerance.
- Two thirds of Belgrade University deans form parallel university authorities and decide to cut off communications with rector Dragutin Velickovic.
- In Belgrade 178 schools are on strike, which is 90 percent of members of the Teachers' Trade Union of Belgrade, says union leader Jagos Bulatovic.
- Serbian government adopts plan for payment of autumn crops, bulk of the debt, 400 million dinars, to be provided by oil, cigarette and wine producers.
- Independent metal workers' trade unions threaten to bring workers in front of government building on February 3 if outstanding wages are not paid by Friday.

- According to a poll conducted by the institute of Social sciences on a sample of 2,040 the majority (26 percent) see the way out of Serbia's crisis in recognition of November 17 local election results.
- Serbian Prime minister to announce new government next week, paper learns.

- Belgrade mayor Nebojisa Covic refuses to open Belgrade's International Film Festival on Friday to symbolically show he is against annulment of local election results according to which he should not longer be in this post.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Political crisis in Serbia should be ended by strictly respecting the will of the people, says Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic during his visit to Montenegro.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Belgrade International Film Festival opens tonight - runs until February 9.
